title: Microtoken inspector flowbook & wireframes
body:
Purpose:
A compact flowbook for a new console panel: the Microtoken Inspector.
Goal: let engineers and SREs inspect single invocations token-by-token (or aggregated slices) to attribute latency and per-token cost, diagnose cache behavior, and compare variants. This should be a light-weight panel that slots into per-route pages and the per-request drilldown.

Top-level UX ideas (high-level):
- Playback-first: scrub a request timeline to see where time/cost accumulates.
- Two modes: "single-invocation" (token-by-token playback) and "slice-aggregate" (percentile/boxplot per-token-position across sample set).
- Compact summary bar: total tokens, billed tokens, estimated $ cost, p95 latency, cache-hit rate.
- Toggle to overlay model/quantization variant so you can compare same request across model variants.

Key interactions (user stories):
- As an ML engineer, I want to scrub a single request and see which tokens (prompt vs generated) caused the latency spike so I can tune prompts or routing.
- As a platform owner, I want to compare two model variants per-token to evaluate cost-latency tradeoffs.
- As an SRE, I want to export token-level traces for a set of failing invocations to attach to an incident.

Data contract (minimal fields required from backend):
- request_id (string)
- route (string)
- user_id (string|nullable)
- model_variant (string)
- timestamp_start (iso)
- tokens: array of {pos:int, text:string, latency_ms:float, cost_usd:float, cache_hit:bool, kernel: string}  // we will accept compressed arrays if large
- total_prompt_tokens:int, total_completion_tokens:int
- billing_tokens:int
- kv_cache_prefetched:boolean
- notes: string (optional)

Sample API snippet (informal):
{
  request_id: "r-1234",
  model_variant: "rw-13b-q4f",
  route: "/chat/completions",
  tokens: [ {pos:0, text:"The", latency_ms:1.8, cost_usd:0.0000002, cache_hit:false}, ... ]
}

Low-fidelity wireframes (components):
1) Header strip (compact): left: back + request-id; center: summary chips (tokens, cost, p95); right: variant dropdown + export button.
2) Timeline scrubber: horizontal time axis with per-token ticks sized by latency (bar height) and colored by cache_hit (green) vs compute (purple). Hover shows token text + latency + cost. Play/pause steps through tokens with 50ms throttle.
3) Token detail pane (below timeline): focuses on selected token, shows text, surrounding window (+-3 tokens), stacktrace pointer (kernel name), kernel-level runtime, GPU/CPU fallback note. Buttons: pin token, add annotation, create issue (Jira).
4) Aggregate view toggle (right rail): switches timeline into boxplot per position across sampled invocations. Controls to choose sample window (last 1k invocations, last 24 hours, custom).
5) Comparison overlay: choose baseline variant and compare per-token heatmap (delta cost and delta latency).

Visual encoding notes:
- Latency = bar height (ms) with log-scale option for long tails.
- Cost = thin overlay line (USD) normalized to panel width (secondary axis).
- Cache hits = green tick; misses = purple.
- Token text is truncated; hover shows full token + byte length.
- When showing aggregate, show p50/p75/p95 whiskers and outlier dots.

Accessibility:
- Scrubber keyboard controls: left/right to step, space to play/pause, home/end to jump to start/end.
- All tokens focusable with ARIA labels for token position and metrics.

Rollout strategy & telemetry:
- Feature gate behind console.experimental.microtoken_inspector.
- Opt-in beta for Dedicated customers (telemetry hooks to measure usage and heavy payload sizes).
- Track: open_count, play_count, export_count, compare_overlay_used, avg_tokens_per_session.

Backlog groom (rough):
- M1 (MVP): single-invocation playback + header + export CSV (T-shirt: M). Acceptance: can load requests up to 2k tokens, scrub, export CSV.
- M2: aggregate slice view + sample selection + p95 boxplots (T-shirt: L). Acceptance: show percentile plots for chosen window and match offline-pagination numbers.
- M3: variant overlay + diff heatmap + per-route integration (T-shirt: L). Acceptance: stable compare UI with toggle.
- M4: annotations + create-jira + long-tail async fetch (T-shirt: S).
- M5: enable streaming token updates (when backend supports incremental token trace) (T-shirt: XL).

Open questions / trade-offs (notes-to-self):
- Should we store full token-by-token traces long-term? (Storage cost high). Proposal: keep 7d raw traces, roll to sampled aggregates for 90d.
- How to surface billing vs estimated cost differences when customers have committed pricing? Add a note: "estimated cost" and link to per-customer pricing model.
- For aggregated views, what is the canonical position index? Some models produce subtokens; we need normalization (byte offsets vs token positions).
- Privacy: ensure PII redaction toggle before export.

Edge cases to design for:
- Very long prompts (10k tokens): timeline compaction mode (group into buckets, allow zoom-in).
- Cache-prefilled responses (zero compute latency): show special badge and skip heavy rendering.
- Mixed-fidelity traces: some requests missing per-token cost (backend sampling). Show partial mode with clear "estimated" tag.

Mock microcopy & inline labels:
- Header chip: "Billed: 128 tokens | est $0.0032 | p95 420ms"
- Timeline hover: "pos 34 — \"assistant\" — 18ms — $0.000002 — cache miss"
- Export dialog: "Include PII? [YES/NO] — Default: NO — Export format: CSV / JSONL"

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Load single request trace within 2s for requests <= 2k tokens over a normal network.
- Playback scrubbing shows latency and cost hover for each token.
- CSV export contains token, pos, latency_ms, cost_usd, cache_hit, kernel.
- Role-based access: only users with "view-invocation-traces" see the panel.

QA checklist (quick):
- [ ] Clip long token text correctly and show hover.
- [ ] Keyboard scrub works in all browsers.
- [ ] Export respects PII toggle.
- [ ] Aggregate percentiles match offline eval harness.

Notes for infra & backend (hand-off):
- Backend should support a compressed token array (delta-encoded latencies) to keep payloads small.
- Provide summary header to avoid fetching full trace on first load (lazy-load token array).
- Add a lightweight endpoint: /requests/:id/trace-summary and /requests/:id/trace-full.

Grooming decisions (from meeting 2025-12-03):
- MVP approved with experimental flag. Design to start with static mock data. Backend work to expose summary endpoint is P0.
- Product prioritized M1 -> M2 in next two sprints.

Todos (short):
- [ ] Design: make low-fidelity mock clickable (Lena) — due 2026-01-05
- [ ] Backend: implement summary endpoint (Samir) — due 2026-01-20
- [ ] Eng: wire the panel to per-route page (Noah) — due 2026-02-02
- [ ] Security review for export (security team) — due 2026-02-09

End of doc.

(If this doc becomes canonical, move to Confluence and link designs. Keep Drive as working notes.)
